corrections: Web does have an indicator. The Text component of the assistant message is MarkdownText (thread.tsx:396), which imports '@assistant-ui/react-markdown/styles/dot.css' (markdown-text.tsx:3). While the assistant message is running and has no parts, assistant-ui renders that empty Text as a placeholder, and dot.css adds a pulsing ● dot to it (rule .aui-md[data-status=running]:empty::after). The difference is purely stylistic: a pulsing dot versus mobile's three-dot bubble (ChatScreen.tsx:208-227; components/chat/TypingIndicator.tsx). assistant-ui's internal behavior could not be verified locally because there are no node_modules.

mobile_evidence: App.tsx:329-330 (useWidgetLanguageRefresh, useIOSWidgetLanguageRefresh); targets/android-widget/kotlin/.../WidgetLocale.kt.tmpl, WidgetLocaleApi33.kt.tmpl; targets/widget/en.lproj
platform_notes: Android uses its own resources and locale for Glance. iOS uses Localizable.strings and reloads via ExtensionStorage.
corrections: The refresh exists (App.tsx:329-330), but it only distinguishes English and Polish. Both hooks reduce the effective language to 'en' or 'pl': useWidgetLanguageRefresh.ts:40-41 and useIOSWidgetLanguageRefresh.ts:54-55 (i18n.resolvedLanguage === 'pl' ? 'pl' : 'en'), and deduplicate on that value, even though the app ships 37 languages (SparkyFitnessMobile/locales). Consequences: (1) switching between two languages other than en or pl (for example de→es) reloads nothing. (2) On Android 13 or later, that 'en' is stored as the priority render cache (WidgetLocale.kt.tmpl:92-95, 221-225), so with a language such as German or Spanish the Glance widgets may render in English until an ACTION_LOCALE_CHANGED corrects it. (3) On iOS only the calories and macros timelines are reloaded (useIOSWidgetLanguageRefresh.ts:67, 76), not the water one or the controls; WidgetKit does resolve its own native locale. The workout Live Activity is repainted with the actual language on languageChanged (workoutLiveActivity.ios.ts:488-497) and supports all languages (resolveLanguage in workoutLiveActivityLabels.ts:87-91).

update_notes: Android now has a Wear OS app with the same pages as the Apple Watch app (goals, water, medications, weight, trend, workout, Now Playing, fasting and steps). It logs and edits strength sets, records runs and walks on the watch with intervals, alerts, auto-pause and voice cues, and shows and controls the phone's GPS recording. It follows the page order, hidden pages and Goals nutrients set on the phone, which shows a 'Wear OS' settings row and the watch option in Record Activity once a Wear OS watch has connected. Unlike the Apple Watch app it has no double tap and no keypad-or-crown setting (rotary input and keypad both work), and per-set RPE only goes from 5 to 10. It also asks for no effort rating at the end, saves nothing to a health app, estimates calories from heart rate and ignores the phone's haptics and rest-alert switches. It cannot follow saved routes, although the phone still offers one when you record outdoors with the watch. As on the Apple Watch, the watch app's text is English only.
